title: [YouPass Collect] - The production of milk annually in four countries
prompt: The table below shows the production of milk annually in four countries in 1990, 2000 and 2010. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates milk manufacturing figures, measured in litres, across four different countries over three specific years: 1990, 2000, and 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while milk production in the Netherlands remained relatively stable and Australia experienced a decline, both Tanzania and Guatemala showed increasing trends during the period. Additionally, the Netherlands and Australia produced significantly more milk than the other two nations, with their output being over 100 times greater.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the major producers, in 1990, the Netherlands and Australia had similar production levels of approximately 11.2 million litres each. The Netherlands maintained steady production throughout the period, with only minor fluctuations, ending at about 11.5 million litres in 2010. In contrast, Australia's output declined notably, falling by roughly 2 million litres to reach 9.2 million litres by the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the smaller producers, Tanzania's milk production started at 87,000 litres in 1990, while Guatemala produced just 26,000 litres. Both countries showed consistent growth over the twenty years, with Tanzania's output increasing to 155,000 litres and Guatemala's production more than tripling to 84,000 litres by 2010.
